questions: Should the pattern be applied to each word as a whole (anchored) or can it match a substring within a word? The reference solution uses re.search without word boundaries inside the pattern, but the test patterns include \b boundaries.
If a word matches the pattern multiple times (e.g., overlapping matches), does it count as a match? The reference solution uses re.search which returns at most one match.
Should the reversal of matched words be done per row independently, or across the entire column globally? The reference solution processes each row independently.
What should happen if the column contains NaN values? The reference solution does not handle NaN explicitly; .apply would pass NaN to the helper.
Is the whitespace separating words exactly any whitespace (\s) or just spaces? The reference solution uses split() which splits on any whitespace.
Should the output preserve the original whitespace (e.g., multiple spaces, tabs) exactly? The reference solution rejoins with a single space.
If the pattern matches but the matched word list is empty after filtering (e.g., due to later mutation), what should happen? The reference solution uses pop(0) which assumes enough matches.
Should the function be case-sensitive? The reference solution uses re.search without flags, so it depends on the pattern.
